finding: A register on dev that is not valid UTF-8 makes crap-score end with a UnicodeDecodeError traceback and exit 1, not with exit 2. The gate-check step reads exit 1 as a failing gate (BR-134), so the developer agent of the story gets a counted attempt for a fault in a file that only the stakeholder writes. The cause is the helper git() at line 562: it decodes the output of git show in text mode with the strict decoder, and read_register at line 721 now passes it a file that a person edits by hand, for example a Reason saved in Latin-1. The review checked the decoder with subprocess.run(..., text=True) on a file that holds the byte 0xE4: it raises UnicodeDecodeError. BR-133 gives exit 2 for every case in which the gate cannot measure, so the behavior looks unintended. Fix: in git(), catch UnicodeDecodeError and raise GateError with the git arguments, or run git with capture_output and decode stdout as UTF-8 inside a try. Add a CG-05-IT-01 case that commits a register with the byte 0xE4 on dev and asserts exit 2 and no report.
why_this_severity: The script exists only on the feature branch, so it is not in use. The case needs a register that is not UTF-8, and the repository's editors and mdformat write UTF-8, so the required behavior holds for every register the project produces (no to fails_purpose). When the case happens, a story loses an attempt and a person must read a traceback to find the cause.
